messages:
alex: Heads-up, hit a subtle correctness gap in staging during a hot-slab reassignment. small window where stale reads were served after an eviction. repro below.

priya: can you summarize the gap?

alex: tl;dr: tenant A had lease token, slab moved to tenant B, B wrote new values. A reused token and got old value for ~150ms before metadata update. Not huge but violates R-A-W for a tiny subset of paths.

sam: that implies tokens/signatures aren't implicitly revoked on handoff. are we checking epoch on read?

alex: runtime checks prefix metadata epoch but metadata propagation lagged. clients keep token and assume it's authoritative.

morgan: options I see: (a) invalidate tokens at handoff via broadcast, (b) bind signatures to per-slab key and rotate on handoff, (c) mark slab as quiescing during handoff so cache reads fall back to miss, (d) change client contract to require post-read validation.

priya: tradeoffs: (a) is immediate but needs control-plane reliability; (b) strong but requires key rotation mechanics; (c) cheap and local but causes extra cold reads; (d) breaking for callers.

alex: quick mitigation proposal: implement quiesce flag on handoff and treat any weak-lease tokens as cache-miss while quiescing. Add metrics for quiesce_rate and quiesce_ms.

sam: agree as short-term. Long-term we should do epoched signatures + a verification cache so we don't pay crypto per-read. verify once per token TTL.

morgan: implement plan: 1) quiesce behind FF, canary on 2 nodes; 2) instrument metrics + alert when quiesce > threshold; 3) RFC for epoched sigs and per-sig verification cache.

priya: detail question: where to keep per-slab keys for sigs? ideally the slab owner keeps the key; on handoff we rotate so old tokens invalid. need to ensure rotation propagation doesn't become the new race.

alex: combine approaches: quiesce during handoff + rotate key on successful takeover + cache verified sigs for TTL. that reduces window and amortizes verify cost.

sam: sketch for verify cache:
```
# on issue: token = (lease{slab,S,epoch}, sig = HMAC(key_S, lease))
# on read: if cache.has(sig) && cache[sig] >= lease.epoch -> serve
else verify(sig,key_S) -> cache[sig]=lease.epoch
```

morgan: ops note: quiesce spikes could blow up cold-starts on hot rebalances. add allow_stale opt for callers that can accept it. default remains strict.

infra-bot: suggested rollout: patch runtime to respect quiesce flag (canary), add telemetry, then RFC for signatures.

alex: I'll open a small PR with FF auth and tests simulating reorder so we hit the race.

priya: add unit tests that simulate delayed metadata propagation and assert reads during quiesce yield cache-miss.

sam: i'll review the crypto bits on the RFC.

morgan: update runbook for interpreting quiesce alerts.

alex: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/9901 (WIP). will post when ready.

infra-bot: CI green on canary, scheduled progressive rollout behind FF at 3pm PT.

morgan: thanks, will follow up on RFC after canary data.
